classification.difficultyReason: Classify each labelled segment using supplied options, separating distance direction, gradient sign and speed from steepness. Falling segments require interpreting gradient magnitude, while the horizontal segment has both zero and constant speed.

content.prompt:
Select the correct description for the gradient and speed of each segment of this graph.
The rate of change of distance with respect to time is the gradient.

spec.description: Unscaled qualitative journey graph. A steepens upwards; B rises linearly; C flattens upwards; D is horizontal; E steepens downwards; F falls linearly; G flattens downwards to the time axis. Width increased from the routine starting size to accommodate the complete vertical axis title and seven segment labels.
spec.mathematics: Distance from the start against time; speed is the magnitude of the gradient. Coordinates are drawing coordinates only, with no numerical scale or equation asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Segment labels, semantic curve colours and axis titles are permanent givens; no selected descriptions appear in the question diagram.

answer.short: a: Distance increasing; gradient positive; speed increasing.
answer.worked: A rises and becomes steeper. Distance increases, the gradient is positive and its magnitude increases, so speed increases.

answer.short: b: Distance increasing; gradient positive; speed constant.
answer.worked: B is a straight rising segment. Distance increases and the positive gradient stays constant, so speed is constant.

answer.short: c: Distance increasing; gradient positive; speed decreasing.
answer.worked: C rises but becomes flatter. Distance increases, the gradient is positive and its magnitude decreases, so speed decreases.

answer.short: d: Distance not changing; gradient zero; speed zero and constant.
answer.worked: D is horizontal. Distance does not change and the gradient is zero, so the object is stopped. Tick both Constant and Zero for speed.

answer.short: e: Distance decreasing; gradient negative; speed increasing.
answer.worked: E falls and becomes steeper. Distance decreases and the gradient is negative. Its magnitude increases, so speed increases.

answer.short: f: Distance decreasing; gradient negative; speed constant.
answer.worked: F is a straight falling segment. Distance decreases and the negative gradient stays constant, so speed is constant.

answer.short: g: Distance decreasing; gradient negative; speed decreasing.
answer.worked: G falls but becomes flatter. Distance decreases and the gradient is negative. Its magnitude decreases, so speed decreases.

inlines.text: The direction of the graph gives the sign of the gradient. Speed is the magnitude of that gradient: increasing steepness means increasing speed; a horizontal segment has zero, constant speed.
